 Railway Staff Seek Rs 69,000 Minimum Pay, 6% Annual Increment Under 8th Pay Commission 
 Railway Staff Seek Rs 69,000 Minimum Pay, 6% Annual Increment Under 8th Pay Commission
 BW Online Bureau
 Oct 31, 2026
 # 8th Pay Commission 
 # Indian Railways 
 # NFIR 
 # Railway Employees 
 # Minimum Basic Pay 
 # Salary Revision 
 # Annual Increment 
 # Pension Benefits 
 # Employee Allowances 
 # Central Government Employees 
 NFIR also seeks five promotions during service, higher pension payouts and a threefold increase in allowances
 AI Generated
 The National Federation of Indian Railwaymen (NFIR) has placed an extensive set of compensation demands before the 8th Central Pay Commission, seeking a minimum basic pay of Rs 69,000, a fitment factor of 3.833 and a doubling of the annual increment from 3 per cent to 6 per cent.
 The federation's proposals extend to career progression, pension entitlements and employee benefits. NFIR has sought a minimum financial benefit of Rs 10,000 under the revised increment structure and at least five promotions during an employee's service. It has also called for open-ended pay scales and a separate salary structure that accounts for the arduous and hazardous nature of railway duties.
 The proposed minimum pay and fitment factor would determine the starting point for salary revision, while the demand for a higher annual increment would affect the subsequent progression of basic pay. 
 Distinct Pay Structure 
The federation has sought a pay framework that recognises the specific demands of railway employment. Its proposals include open-ended pay scales and job-specific benefits, alongside a minimum of five promotions during an employee's career.
 The proposed increase in the annual increment from 3 per cent to 6 per cent, subject to a minimum financial benefit of Rs 10,000, forms another component of its pay revision demands.
 NFIR has also called for the integration of DA into basic pay once the allowance reaches the 25 per cent threshold. The proposal would make the specified DA level a trigger for revising the basic pay structure.
 Higher Pension Payouts 
The federation has proposed pension at 67 per cent of the last pay drawn and family pension at 50 per cent. It has also sought a reduction in the commutation recovery period from 15 years to 11 years.
 These demands cover both the pension payable to retired employees and the benefits available to their families. The proposed reduction in the commutation deduction period would shorten the period during which the commuted portion of pension remains subject to recovery.
NFIR has sought the restoration of discontinued allowances and a threefold increase in existing allowances. It has also demanded benefits tailored to specific job responsibilities and the inclusion of employees' parents in the eligibility criteria for railway passes.
